note: 15 numbered high-elevation sites along the Little River, suitable for tents and small to medium RVs.  The narrow gravel road may be tricky for larger rigs.  Very remote with no cell service.  Sites fill up on weekends.  --AWH  Reviews (2020-23, all 5*): about half the ~16 numbered sites on FR 17 take a trailer, and a side loop of 5 gravel-pad sites (turnoff between sites 6 and 7) is the trailer pick. It's often empty even on weekends, while the riverside sites fill. Largest rig reported is a 36-ft fifth wheel, but the road is narrow, potholed and muddy after rain, with tight turns onto one-lane bridges. Sites 9 and 13 are called the prettiest, with small pools and a gravel beach ~50 yd below 9, and wildflowers, ferns and grassy spots at the water. Fire rings and a few tables; no trash service. Daytime helicopter and low-level military jet noise is a recurring complaint. An aggressive black bear was reported in 2023, so keep food locked in the vehicle. --Claude

note: High-elevation dispersed creekside sites at the confluence of Abes Run and the East Fork of the Greenbrier River.  Sites on far side of the river may not be accessible when water is high.  --AWH  There are 4 distinct sites off Abes Run Rd (FR 51), all with fire rings and a view of the river; one has a picnic table. Swimming and fishing are good when the river is low. --Claude

name: Pennyrile Forest State Resort Park
note: Kentucky State Parks (Dawson Springs). ~56 sites, 30/50A electric + water (some full hookups), paved pads, dump, cable; equestrian section has level pull-through hookup sites usable by any RVer. Campground set back from the 56-acre lake. Reserve via Kentucky State Parks. ~Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Big Bone Lick State Historic Site
note: Kentucky State Parks (Union). ~62 paved hilltop sites, electric + water (30A, some full hookup), all back-in, dump, showers, laundry, camp store, playground. Reserve via Kentucky State Parks. ~Apr-Oct, 14-day max. Some sites need long water hoses. --Claude

name: Barren River Lake State Resort Park
note: Kentucky State Parks (Lucas). ~99-101 sites; sites 1-9 full hookup (W/E/S), rest water+electric (30/50A), pull-throughs, max ~60 ft, dump, two playgrounds; wooded peninsula on Barren River Lake (some sites have lake views). Sloped - leveling needed. ~late Apr-mid Nov. Reserve via Kentucky State Parks. --Claude

name: Natural Bridge State Resort Park - Middle Fork Campground
note: Kentucky State Parks (Slade). ~36 water+electric RV sites (20/30/50A, 8 pull-through, max ~45 ft) + ~11 tent-only; B-section sites back to Middle Fork Creek. Dump, showers, camp store. ~Mar-Oct. Reserve via Kentucky State Parks. --Claude

name: Cumberland Falls State Resort Park
note: Kentucky State Parks (Corbin). Ridgeline loop ~49 sites with 21 paved RV pads, water + 10/30/50A electric, dump, grocery, laundry, playground; max RV ~30 ft (a 23-ft fits). Clifty section (~9 sites) is tent-only. On a ridge set back from the Cumberland River. ~mid-Mar-mid-Nov. Reserve via Kentucky State Parks. RV Life 3.5*. NOTE: the campground is closed for the 2026 season for renovations (reopens 2027); park/reservations otherwise via ReserveAmerica. --Claude

name: Grayson Lake State Park
note: Kentucky State Parks (Grayson). 71 sites, 30/50A electric + shared water spigots (bring 35-50 ft hose), no full hookups, max RV ~45-60 ft, single dump, showers; on a ridge set back from Grayson Lake (lake access via trail), adjacent to the golf course. Sloped - leveling needed. ~Apr-Oct. Reserve via Kentucky State Parks. --Claude

name: Kincaid Lake State Park
note: Kentucky State Parks (Falmouth). ~84 standard-electric RV sites (+ 75 tent), 20A electric + water, gravel pads, back-in & some pull-through, large rigs OK, bathhouse, dump; RV loops set back in woods (only some tent sites near the 183-acre lake). ~Mar-Nov 15. Reserve via Kentucky State Parks. --Claude

name: Carr Creek State Park
note: Kentucky State Parks (Sassafras). 39 sites, electric (30A) + water, back-in, max RV ~30-60 ft, bathhouse, dump; adjacent to the longest sand beach in the KY park system on 750-acre Carr Fork Lake (some RV sites have lake views). ~Mar-Nov. Reserve via Kentucky State Parks. --Claude

name: Lake Barkley State Resort Park
note: Kentucky State Parks (Cadiz). ~78 sites (73 standard electric 30A + water, 6 no-hookup), paved back-in (some steep/unlevel), max RV ~32-58 ft, two bathhouses, dump, campers' boat ramp; wooded ravine with many sites overlooking Lake Barkley fingers. ~Apr-Oct. Reserve via Kentucky State Parks. --Claude

name: Kendall Campground
note: USACE Nashville District, Lake Cumberland. Tailwater campground on the Cumberland River just below Wolf Creek Dam (Jamestown), next to Wolf Creek NFH. 116 sites, water+electric (20/30/50A), two heavily wooded loops, 2 bathhouses, 2 dump stations; back-ins + some pull-throughs, pads to ~50 ft (some listed longer). Sites overlook the river (scenic tailwater); not directly on the water. Reserve online. ~Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Waitsboro Campground
note: USACE Nashville District, Lake Cumberland (Somerset). Small: ~17 RV sites (electric) + 5 tent, 8 sites on the waterfront; dump, showers, laundry, boat ramp, playground. Tight exit turnaround - 5th-wheels over 32 ft are warned off, but a 23-ft rig is fine. Reserve online. ~Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Fishing Creek Campground
note: USACE Nashville District, Lake Cumberland (W of Somerset). 26 RV sites + 20 tent, water+electric; boat ramp, dump, showers, laundry. Wooded; many sites sit near/on the water at summer pool (steep inclines down to the lake between areas, sharp entrance). Reserve online. ~Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Fall Creek Campground
note: USACE Nashville District, Lake Cumberland (Monticello). Small lakeside loop: 10 RV sites (water+electric, ~29-70 ft), all waterfront, + dump, boat ramp, playground, showers. Reserve online. ~mid-May to mid-Oct. --Claude

name: Baileys Point Campground
note: USACE Nashville District, Barren River Lake (Lucas/Scottsville). Largest of the lake's Corps campgrounds: 215 sites across 5 loops, most water+electric, bathhouses, dump, laundry, two playgrounds, sand volleyball, amphitheater, boat ramp; loops B & C have many sites facing the lake (some on private coves for mooring). Reserve online. ~Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Axtel Campground
note: USACE Louisville District, Rough River Lake (McDaniels/Falls of Rough). Large: 158 sites, most water+electric, sits directly on the lakeshore with lake views from nearly all sites (waterfront sites book fast); swim beach, boat ramp, dump, showers, playground, fish-cleaning station. Reserve online. ~Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Laurel Branch Campground
note: USACE Louisville District, Rough River Lake (McDaniels). 62 sites (several electric), most waterfront (rest a short walk to the lake); flush toilets, showers, playground, boat ramp, beach, fish-cleaning, nature trail. ~Apr 14-Oct 30. Reserve online. --Claude

name: Buckhorn Campground
note: USACE Louisville District, Buckhorn Lake (Buckhorn), eastern KY Cumberland Plateau. ~30 paved standard-electric sites + walk-in tent and boat-in; 14 waterfront sites at the water's edge. Flush toilets, hot showers, dump, laundry, WiFi, playground, swim area, boat ramp. RVs to ~50 ft. Open ~May 1-Sep 30. Reserve online. --Claude

name: Trace Branch Campground
note: USACE Louisville District, Buckhorn Lake (near Hazard), eastern KY. Mostly-waterfront sites with electric/water (some 50A, some sewer), pads to ~70 ft; shower house, dump, playground, fishing area. Mix of reservable and first-come sites. Open ~May-Sept. --Claude

name: Blue Heron Campground
note: NPS, Big South Fork National River & Recreation Area (Stearns), on the plateau near the Blue Heron historic mining community. 45 sites, all water+electric, back-in + pull-through, pads to ~61 ft; flush toilets, hot showers, dump station. Wooded (not on the water; the river gorge is below the rim). ~Apr-Nov. Reserve online. --Claude

name: Twin Knobs Campground
note: USFS Daniel Boone NF, Cave Run Lake (Salt Lick/Morehead). Large: 200+ sites over 10 loops, electric to full-hookup (premium), paved spurs to ~70 ft, dump, bathhouses, camp store, boat ramp, sandy swim beach; outer-loop sites sit on the lakeshore (waterfront sites book early). ~late Apr-early Nov. Reserve online. --Claude

name: Clear Creek Campground
note: USFS Daniel Boone NF, Clear Creek Recreation Area (Salt Lick), E of Cave Run Lake. Small primitive ~20-site campground along Clear Creek (tent/RV pads, no hookups), vault toilets, drinking water; boat ramp onto Clear Creek Lake + picnic area nearby. Max RV ~30 ft (a 23-ft rig fits); first-come, first-served, no reservations. ~Apr 15-Nov 29. --Claude

name: Holly Bay Campground
note: USFS Daniel Boone NF, Laurel River Lake (Keavy/London), ~2 mi N of Laurel River Dam. ~75 drive-in sites (single + double family), 20/30/50A electric + water, paved pads to ~50 ft, flush toilets, showers; near Holly Bay Marina/boat ramp. Many sites have water views but none directly on the shore. Run by concessionaire American Land & Leisure. ~early Apr-mid Oct. Reserve online. --Claude

name: Wolf River Resort & Marina
note: Private (Albany), on Dale Hollow Lake (end of Hwy 738), operating since 1946. ~30 RV sites with full hookups + cabins, motel, houseboats, marina, restaurant, pool, WiFi. Seasonal ~May-Sept. RV camping is one part of a marina resort. --Claude

name: Guist Creek Marina & Campground
note: Private (Shelbyville), on Guist Creek Lake (Shelbyville's water-supply lake). Pull-through water+electric (30/50A) + primitive sites, shower house, dump, marina/boat ramp; lake-view sites. ~Mar-Nov. --Claude

name: Riverfront Park Campground
note: Riverfront Park on the Ohio River. 16 sites across a field from the river, W/E, dump, free WiFi; two boat ramps, dock, river views. ~Apr 1-Nov 30, 10-day limit, $25. RV Life 4*. --AWH

name: Lake Jericho Recreation Area
note: Henry County park on 137-acre Lake Jericho (est. 1969), under new management with its own website. 62 RV sites with water and electric, about half with sewer; dump station, camp store, lakeside. Roughly Apr-Oct; now booked online through ResNexus (up to 12 months ahead, 27 nights at a time). --Claude

name: Logan-Hubble County Park
note: Local (Garrard County), a 400-acre park/nature preserve between Stanford and Lancaster with a 12-acre lake. 13 gravel water+electric sites; disc golf, trails, shelters. ~Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Fish Pond Lake RV Park
note: Local (Letcher County), in 895-acre Little Laurel Park above 45-acre Fish Pond Lake (~1 mi W of Payne Gap, Jenkins). Graveled RV sites (water/sewer/30A), WiFi, restrooms (no showers); set above the lake (lake views, no direct water access), electric-motor/paddle boating. ~Mar-Oct. --Claude

name: Fox Valley Recreation Park
note: Local (Fleming County, Wallingford). 85 gravel sites, RVs to ~45 ft, 20/30A water/electric (some sewer), flush toilets, hot showers, dump, store; many seasonal/permanent sites plus a couple nightly-rental sites and a large primitive area. ~Apr-Oct, 14-day max. --Claude

name: Chain O'Lakes State Park
note: Illinois DNR (Spring Grove), at the Fox River chain of lakes. ~238 sites: Class A electric (Honeysuckle Hollow, Fox Den) + Class B-premium areas (Turner Lake South, Prairie View, Mud Lake East); showers, dump. Some sites by the water. Reserve via ExploreMoreIL. ~Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Kankakee River State Park
note: Illinois DNR (Bourbonnais), on the Kankakee River. Potawatomi Campground: 110 Class A electric sites (showers, dump, flush toilets), RVs to ~35 ft; + Chippewa (Class BE/C). Wooded, set back from the river. Reserve via ExploreMoreIL. ~Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Apple River Canyon State Park
note: Illinois DNR (Apple River, NW IL). Canyon Ridge Campground: 49 Class C primitive sites (no hookups), pit toilets, water spigots, dump station, no showers; $8. ~mid-Apr to Oct, reservable + FCFS via ExploreMoreIL. Winding canyon access. --Claude

name: Giant City State Park
note: Illinois DNR (Makanda), Shawnee hill country. 85 Class A electric sites (9 50A, rest 30A), water, showers, dump, privies; ~half reservable, rest FCFS via silent-host. $20. Reserve via ExploreMoreIL (closed Dec-Mar). --Claude

name: Saline County State Fish and Wildlife Area
note: Illinois DNR (Equality), overlooking Glen O Jones Lake. 45 sites, no electric/water hookups (water spigot near #31), trailer dump, pads 40-45 ft; boat ramp, swimming. First-come, first-served, ~Apr-Sept. RV Life unrated. --Claude

name: Horseshoe Lake State Park (Madison County)
note: Illinois DNR (Granite City), on a 2,400-acre Mississippi oxbow lake (Walker's Island). Semi-primitive: 26 sites, no electric/showers, water hydrants, dump, outhouses; $8. ~May-Sept. Distinct from Horseshoe Lake in Alexander County. --Claude  Closed until May 2027: IDNR says the campground and its road are closed for a causeway project (read 2026-10-12). --Claude

name: Nauvoo State Park
note: Illinois DNR (Nauvoo), near the Mississippi River; campground around 13-acre Lake Horton. 105 sites (35 Class A, 70 Class B), 30A electric (some water/sewer), showers, RVs to ~60 ft. ~Apr-Oct. Reserve via ExploreMoreIL. --Claude

name: Deer Run Campground (Sangchris Lake State Park)
note: Illinois DNR (Rochester), north side of Sangchris Lake. Deer Run Campground: 80 Class A electric sites (showers, dump) + 40 primitive + tent + equestrian; set in woods (not directly waterfront - Hickory Point is the lakefront campground, separately in DB). Closed mid-Jan to Mar. Reserve via ExploreMoreIL. --Claude

name: Woodford State Fish and Wildlife Area
note: Illinois DNR (Low Point), on Illinois River backwater lakes (Goose Lake / Upper Peoria Lake). 12 seasonal drive-in sites near the boat ramps, no hookups, max RV ~30 ft; sheltered tables, pit toilets, fire pits. First-come, ~Apr-Sept. RV Life unrated. --Claude

name: Blanchard Island Recreation Area
note: USACE Rock Island District, Mississippi River (New Boston). Small/primitive: 15 sites (table/fire ring, vault toilets; a couple of host sites have water/electric), boat ramp, view of Blanchard Chute. First-come 'Scan & Pay', ~May 15-Oct 15. RV Life unrated. --Claude

name: Pine Ridge Campground (Pounds Hollow)
note: USFS Shawnee NF, on the ridgetop above Pounds Hollow Lake (Karbers Ridge). 13 electric (20/30/50A) + 22 non-electric sites, water spigot, $10 cash/check. Narrow undulating roads limit rigs to UNDER ~25 ft - a 23-ft fits but big rigs don't. FCFS, ~Mar 15-Dec 15. --Claude

name: Redbud Campground (Bell Smith Springs)
note: USFS Shawnee NF, Bell Smith Springs Recreation Area (Ozark/Eddyville). 21 sites, no hookups, vault toilets, one potable-water source; accommodates pull-behinds/motorhomes to ~24 ft (a 23-ft fits; best for compact rigs). FCFS, $10, ~Mar 15-Dec 15. --Claude

name: Crab Orchard Campground (Crab Orchard NWR)
note: USFWS Crab Orchard National Wildlife Refuge (Marion), on Crab Orchard Lake; concessionaire-run (Bluegill Bay). 62 RV + 7 tent sites, full-hookup / electric-water / non-electric, showers, dump, flush toilets, small camper beach; many waterfront sites, RVs to ~38 ft. First-come, ~Apr 1-mid Nov. --Claude

name: Pine Hills Campground (Shawnee NF)
note: USFS Shawnee NF (Wolf Lake), by the LaRue-Pine Hills bottoms. 13 level primitive sites, no hookups, vault toilets, no potable water (bring your own); max RV length ~80 ft but no pull-throughs. FCFS, $10, ~Mar 15-Dec 15. RV Life unrated. --Claude

name: Tower Rock Campground (Shawnee NF)
note: USFS Shawnee NF (Elizabethtown), on the bank of the Ohio River. Free primitive campground, pit toilet, no water/electric; improved sites take small trailers/RVs (~25 ft; a 23-ft fits). Flood-prone with river levels. ~May 1-Dec 15, 14-day max. RV Life unrated. --Claude

name: Blackwell Family Campground
note: Local (Forest Preserve District of DuPage County, in Blackwell FP, Warrenville). 60+ drive-in electric sites (tents/trailers/motorhomes), crushed-limestone pads, showers, dump + water-fill (no hookups). Silver Lake in preserve but not RV-site-adjacent (waterfront none). Weekends-only May-Columbus Day; reservations. --Claude

name: Illiniwek Forest Preserve
note: Local (Rock Island County Forest Preserve District, Hampton) on the Mississippi. 60 water/electric RV pads + dump station + 2 shower houses; 25 primitive sites near the shore are tent-only. RV loops set back with river views (waterfront riverview). Seasonal Apr-Oct; first-come-first-served (permit at camp office). --Claude

name: Loud Thunder Forest Preserve
note: Local (Rock Island County Forest Preserve District, Illinois City). RV camping in White Oak (26 water/electric sites) + Deer Haven (35 full-hookup 50A pull-throughs); showers, marina/boat rental on 167-acre Lake George, 12+ mi trails; separate equestrian loop. RV loops not on the water (waterfront none). Reservable, 2-night min, Apr-Oct. RV Life ~9/10. RV Life mislabels state; it is county FP. --Claude

name: Friends Creek Conservation Area
note: Local (Macon County Conservation District, near Decatur). ~35-40 sites (mostly 30/50A electric, 3 non-electric), showers/flush toilets/dump station; some back-in sites are short but 50A service handles larger rigs. Season ~May-Nov; reservations. --Claude

name: South Park Municipal Campground
note: Local (City of Gibson City, in South Park at IL-9/Lott Blvd; some directories list this as 'Arrowsmith Park & Campground' — same place). 9 asphalt sites incl. 1 ADA pull-through, 30A electric + water, fire rings, restroom/showers, dump station. Apr-Oct, 7-night limit, ~$10-20; first-come-first-served, self-pay (shower keys at Police Dept). --Claude

name: Robinson City Park
note: Local (City of Robinson Parks & Rec). 8 sites (first 3-4 with concrete pads), 20/50A electric + water spigot + dump station, pool/showers in park; $25/night. Open May-Sept; first-come-first-served, 3-night limit, pay at the pool. --Claude

name: Francis Park
note: Local (City of Kewanee). 60 RV sites (30x 30A, 30x 20A), central water fill + dump station, restrooms (no showers); $13/night. No water body at the park (waterfront none). First-come-first-served for electric sites; season closes ~end of August. --Claude

name: Allison Campground
note: Local (City of Galesburg) at Lake Storey Recreation Area. 142 sites (21 full-hookup, 101 electric/some water, 41 primitive/tent), concrete pads, dump station, adjacent water park/beach/golf. Official site map shows RV sites behind a wooded buffer, none on the shoreline (waterfront none). Season ~Apr-mid Oct; reservations by phone/in-person. RV Life mislabels commercial; it is municipal. --Claude

name: Great River Road Campground
note: Local (Pleasant Hill area, Pike County; adjoins the Pike County Fairgrounds but operates as a standalone public campground, not event-only). 59 full-hookup sites (E/W/S 30/50A), 40 pull-throughs, 60-ft max, dump station; inland by the fairgrounds (waterfront none). Open Apr-Oct; reservations by phone. --Claude

name: Mahlon Dickerson Reservation
note: Morris County Park Commission; 18 paved back-in RV sites with electric (15/30/50 amp) and seasonal water (May 1–Oct 1), largest to ~40 ft; tent and Adirondack-shelter sites separate; highest-elevation campground in NJ; 14-night max; open Apr–Nov; reservable online. --Claude

name: Pomme de Terre State Park - Hermitage
note: Hermitage-side campground on Pomme de Terre Lake with basic and electric sites; flat, open, grassy terrain reviewers prefer for larger rigs; open Mar-Nov; reservable online. --Claude

name: Aunts Creek
note: USACE Table Rock Lake campground on the James River Arm, 55 electric/water sites with hot showers and a dump station; reservable online (open May-mid-Sep). --Claude

name: Indian Point
note: Large USACE Table Rock Lake campground ~8 mi from Branson (74 sites, mostly electric+water) with many lakefront sites, a swim beach, boat ramp and marina; reservable online Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Viola
note: USACE Table Rock Lake campground on the Kings River Arm at Shell Knob (~56 sites, ~42 electric) including waterfront pads, plus the Kings River Marina; access roads can be rough for larger rigs; reservable online Apr-Sep. --Claude

name: Beaver Creek
note: USACE Bull Shoals Lake campground on the Beaver Creek arm near Forsyth, 33 electric/water sites (paved spurs to ~42 ft) with a swim beach; reservable online Apr-Sep. --Claude

name: Theodosia Park
note: USACE Bull Shoals Lake campground at Theodosia, 26 electric sites across two loops with a marina, swim area and boat ramp; reservable online May-Sep. --Claude

name: Lane Spring Recreation Area
note: USFS Mark Twain NF campground on Little Piney Creek (trout stream) near Rolla; 17 sites (6 electric, 11 basic) with 6 creekside, RVs to ~34 ft; sites are FCFS (only the group pavilion is reservable); open Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Paddy Creek Recreation Area
note: USFS Mark Twain NF campground nestled along Paddy Creek near Licking; 19 non-electric sites (asphalt pads to ~34 ft), no potable water; FCFS via fee tube; open Apr-Dec. --Claude

name: Loggers Lake
note: USFS Mark Twain NF campground on spring-fed Logger's Lake near Bunker; ~14 non-electric sites all with lake views; reservable online; the final access road is rough (high-clearance recommended); open Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Council Bluff Recreation Area
note: USFS Mark Twain NF campground at 440-acre Council Bluff Lake (largest lake in the forest) near Belgrade; non-electric drive-in sites (some to ~40 ft) plus walk-ins, with a swim beach and lake-loop trail; reservable online; open Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Red Bluff Recreation Area
note: USFS Mark Twain NF campground along Huzzah Creek near Davisville; 44 sites (6 electric) with some sites close to the creek; reservable online; open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Marble Creek Recreation Area
note: USFS Mark Twain NF campground on Marble Creek near Fredericktown (Ozark Trail trailhead); 26 non-electric sites, 6 directly creekside, no potable water; FCFS via fee tube; open Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Dry Fork Recreation Area
note: USFS Mark Twain NF campground at the Cedar Creek Trail trailhead near New Bloomfield; 8 non-electric drive-in sites (to ~30 ft) plus a group site, potable water and vault toilet; FCFS; open Apr-Dec. --Claude

name: Pine Ridge Recreation Area
note: Small USFS Mark Twain NF pine-forest campground in the Cedar Creek district near New Bloomfield; 8 non-electric sites (2 fit ~34-ft RVs, the rest smaller), potable water and vault toilet; FCFS; open Apr-Dec. --Claude

name: Watercress Recreation Area
note: USFS Mark Twain NF campground on the banks of the Current River at Van Buren; 17 non-electric sites (RVs to 40 ft) with drinking water and a boat launch; FCFS; open May-Oct. --Claude

name: Float Camp Recreation Area
note: USFS Mark Twain NF campground ~150 ft from the Current River near Doniphan; some 30/50A electric and many non-electric sites (RVs to 40 ft) with pressurized water; individual sites are FCFS; open ~Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Deer Leap Recreation Area
note: Small, quiet USFS campground on the east bank of the Current River near Doniphan; 7 non-electric sites (28-ft max), drinking water and vault toilet; FCFS; open Apr-Dec. --Claude

name: Markham Springs Recreation Area
note: USFS Mark Twain NF campground on the Black River near Ellsinore; a 50A electric loop (Birch) plus three non-electric loops, with showers and drinking water; reservable online May-Labor Day, FCFS otherwise; open May-Oct. --Claude

name: Pinewoods Lake Recreation Area
note: USFS Mark Twain NF campground at 31-acre Pinewoods Lake near Ellsinore; 15 paved sites (mostly non-electric with a limited electric option), RVs to ~30 ft; reservable online; open Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: North Fork Recreation Area
note: USFS Mark Twain NF campground above the North Fork of the White River near Dora; 19 non-electric sites (trailers mostly under 30 ft, some to 34 ft); FCFS; open May-Dec. --Claude

name: Blue Springs Lake Campground
note: Jackson County Parks campground at Blue Springs Lake (Fleming Park) with 82 sites (30 full-hookup, 13 electric+water, 39 electric-only, 20/30/50A); reservable online, open Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Lake Jacomo Campground
note: Jackson County Parks campground on Lake Jacomo in Fleming Park with ~57 sites incl. full-hookup and electric (20/30/50A); a few sites have a lake view; reservable online, open Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Longview Lake Campground
note: Jackson County Parks campground near 930-acre Longview Lake with 89 sites (17 full-hookup, 59 electric, 12 tent), showers and a dump station; reservable online, open Apr-Sep. --Claude

name: Shelbina Lake Campground
note: City of Shelbina park on Shelbina Lake with ~90 FCFS electric sites (mostly 30/50A) at $25/night paid at the golf pro shop or City Hall; open late Mar-Oct. --Claude

name: Hidden Valley Outfitters Overnight RV Park
note: Outfitter's RV park on the Niangua River next to Bennett Spring State Park (open Mar-Oct): a grid of level concrete full-hookup pads beside the river, with the outfitter's store, float trips, cabins and a tent campground. --Claude

name: Running River Canoe Rental
note: Upper Current River float outfitter near Salem with 12 full-hookup RV sites set back from the river; seasonal (~May-Sep), reservable by phone. --Claude

name: Deer Rest Camp Park
note: Family-owned Warsaw campground near Truman Lake/Drake Harbor with 46+ full-hookup sites (30/50A); seasonal Mar-Nov, reservable. --Claude

name: Majestic Oaks Park
note: Lake of the Ozarks-area campground near Eldon with 80 sites (32 full-hookup, 30/50A), pool and trails; open Apr-Nov, reservable. --Claude

name: Chipmunk Crossing RV Park
note: Quiet 17-site RV park (14 full-hookup) outside West Plains; open Apr-Oct, reservable. --Claude

name: Prairie Dog State Park

season.note: ReserveAmerica: campsites reservable April 1 - October 31, certain sites open through December 31; facility status 'Open year round'. Water is shut off from about mid-October to mid-April.

note: NW-side campground complex at Pueblo Reservoir. Loops sit on the plains terrace above a rocky/cliff shore (not sandy beach); closer Yucca Flats sites overlook the lake (lakeview). Named swim beach is a separate day-use area. --Claude

name: San Luis Lakes State Wildlife Area (Mosca)

The lake itself is currently dry. FCFS, but everyone 16+ must carry a CPW SWA pass or current Colorado hunting/fishing license. --Claude

name: Stagecoach State Park (Junction City)

name: Stagecoach State Park (Harding Spur)
note: Stagecoach State Park loop on the Harding Cove inlet at the north end of Stagecoach Reservoir, near the marina; sites run parallel to the open shore and reviewers tie boats up at their site. --Claude

Length conflict (2026-10-28): the campground page gives parking lengths of 15-30 ft and says this older facility will not take larger RVs, but the forest's campground-status table lists a 20-ft maximum spur. --Claude Online photos show at least a few sites that can take EKKO, but reviews say the sites are short and unlevel: have a backup plan. --AWH 2026-10-28
